name: Vet Atlas placeholder geometry
notes: Schematic shapes generated by the build scripts where no scan exists yet (fidelity "illustrative"): costal cartilages, the dens of the axis and the xiphoid cartilage in scripts/build-dog-skeletal.ts. Not anatomically accurate.

name: 3D Dog Bone Project, Massey University (School of Veterinary Science and Institute of Natural and Mathematical Sciences), nzfauna on Sketchfab
notes: Structured-light scans (DAVID SLS-2, 0.2 mm) of left-side bones of one dog, assembled in anatomical position. Individual bones: femur, hip bone, humerus, scapula, ulna, C7, L1, upper skull and lower jaw are CC BY-SA; tibia, fibula, radius and atlas are CC BY-NC. Downloaded and decimated by scripts/build-dog-skeletal.ts; right-side bones are mirrored copies.

name: VetAgro Sup Anatomy, Lyon (VASAnatomy on Sketchfab)
notes: Photogrammetry of plastinated specimens. Used: 'Ensemble Larynx et appareil Hyoide de chien' (hyoid apparatus with larynx).

name: Chair of Anatomy, Histology and Embryology, LMU Munich (vetanatMunich on Sketchfab)
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (most models; a few are CC BY 4.0)
notes: Checked 2026-09-13 via the Sketchfab API: 207 of 220 downloadable models are ND and cannot be used. Only the 13 CC BY models (horse teeth, donkey tarsus, dog manubrium, mink atlas) are eligible. Used: manubrium sterni dog (CC BY 4.0, Artec Micro scan); it is also the base the sternebrae 2–7 and the xiphoid process are derived from (fidelity "modeled").

name: Veterinary Histology, The Ohio State University (Jennings & Premanandan)
Wikimedia Commons
license: Per file (CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain)
notes: Record the exact license and author of each file in its media entry.

name: MorphoSource, Felis catus CT series (3D Anatomy Studios)
notes: Whole-body microCT of one cat (3DAS:00001, media 000360675 and 000360846) and loose cat bones. Checked 2026-10-09: every Felis catus media uses the MorphoSource Standard use agreement (InC-NC), which forbids republishing derivatives without permission. Not used; ask 3D Anatomy Studios (Aaron Olsen) for permission before integrating.

name: "Canine Model" by Lova Dahn (lovadahn on Sketchfab)
notes: Hand-sculpted, retopologised dog/wolf base mesh (author tags it 'notaigenerated'). License checked 2026-10-08 via the Sketchfab API. Only the body and claw meshes are used: scripts/build-dog-integumentary.ts bends the tail down and registers the body onto the dog skeleton with a thin-plate-spline warp driven by skeletal landmarks, then pushes the surface clear of the bones (fidelity "modeled").

name: Vet Atlas procedural musculature
notes: Muscles modelled procedurally by scripts/build-dog-muscular.ts, scripts/build-cat-muscular.ts and scripts/build-cow-muscular.ts (fidelity "illustrative"): origins and insertions are landmarks measured on each species' skeletal model, bellies are lofted tubes and slabs following standard veterinary anatomy texts. Schematic shapes; topography (attachments, relative size, layering) is the teaching goal, not exact morphology.

name: "3D Canine Anatomy: Normal Abdomen" by pixelbeaker (Sketchfab)
notes: CT segmentation of one dog (caudal thorax to hips). License checked 2026-10-08 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-dog-visceral.ts + scripts/ct/visceral.py use the liver, stomach (fundus and body), small intestine, kidneys, abdominal great vessels and the caudal half of the lungs; its ribs, vertebrae and pelvis only register the organs to the skeleton. Surfaces are closed by voxel morphology, decimated and rescaled per axis to the skeleton's body proportions; the great vessels are bent along the spine and the lungs extended cranially (fidelity "modeled" for those).

name: "Normal Canine Heart Anatomy" by pixelbeaker (Sketchfab)
notes: CT segmentation of the heart and great-vessel roots of a large-breed dog. License checked 2026-10-08 via the Sketchfab API. Registered by ICP onto the heart remnant of the abdomen CT, vessels trimmed near the base, rescaled and decimated by scripts/ct/visceral.py.

name: Cortical Atlas of the Canine Brain (Johnson & Barry 2019, Cornell University eCommons)
notes: MRI population template of 30 mesaticephalic/dolichocephalic dogs with tissue and ROI label maps. CC0; the authors ask to be cited: Johnson, Philippa J. and Erica F. Barry (2019) Cortical Atlas of the Canine Brain [dataset]. scripts/ct/brain.py meshes the brain mask (cerebrum, cerebellum from the atlas labels, brainstem); scripts/ct/visceral.py fits it into the cranial cavity of the skull scan.

name: Vet Atlas procedural organs
notes: Organs without a usable open scan, modelled by scripts/ct/visceral.py (dog), scripts/ct/cat_visceral.py (cat) and scripts/ct/cow_visceral.py (cow: every organ but the stomach and heart, including the brain, liver, lungs, kidneys, uterus and ovaries) (fidelity "illustrative"): trachea and principal bronchi, esophagus, pancreas, spleen, large intestine, urinary bladder, prostate and thyroid lobes, as tubes, ribbons and ellipsoids placed from skeletal landmarks and the scanned organs. Schematic shapes; topography is the teaching goal.

name: Greyhound pelvic limb CT scan, John Hutchinson (Royal Veterinary College), figshare
notes: DICOM CT of one greyhound pelvis and pelvic limb (three series). Bone surfaces extracted by scripts/ct/greyhound_hindlimb.py (threshold, watershed, marching cubes), scaled to the Massey skeleton and registered on its tibia, femur and hip bone by scripts/build-dog-skeletal.ts. Used for the patella, tarsus, metatarsus, pelvic phalanges, sacrum and caudal vertebrae.

name: Front leg of a dog, Scan the World (MyMiniFactory), Zenodo record 21487908
notes: Surface from a medical CT of a dog forelimb (one closed mesh). Split into bones by scripts/ct/stw_front_leg.py (voxelisation and watershed), mirrored to a left limb, scaled and placed under the Massey radius by scripts/build-dog-skeletal.ts. Used for the carpus, metacarpus and thoracic phalanges.

name: Dog Baculum, SusanElaineJones on Sketchfab
notes: 3D scan of an isolated os penis; scaled and placed by hand in scripts/build-dog-skeletal.ts.

name: "Feline Skeleton Dec" by westerly (Sketchfab)
notes: Complete feline skeleton sculpted in ZBrush from reference (not a scan), with every bone as a separate shell. License checked 2026-10-09 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-cat-skeletal.ts splits it into bones, rescales it to a domestic cat and replaces its skull and mandible with RISD scans (fidelity "modeled").

name: Edna Lawrence Nature Lab, Rhode Island School of Design (RISD Nature Lab on Sketchfab)
notes: Artec Spider structured-light scans of specimens in the Nature Lab collection. License checked 2026-10-09 via the Sketchfab API. Used for the cat (scripts/build-cat-skeletal.ts): the skull is the scanned left half of one cranium mirrored and closed at the midline (the full skull scan of the same specimen lacks teeth and zygomatic arches); the mandible is a different, smaller specimen scaled up 26% to fit. Both are registered onto the sculpted feline skeleton and decimated.

name: "Cat Model" by Lova Dahn (Sketchfab)
notes: Hand-sculpted, retopologised domestic cat base mesh with separate eyes and claws, by the author of the dog base mesh. License checked 2026-10-09 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-cat-integumentary.ts registers the body onto the cat skeleton with a thin-plate-spline warp driven by skeletal landmarks (fidelity "modeled").

name: "Normal Feline Anatomy – Digestive System" by pixelbeaker (Sketchfab)
notes: CT segmentation of one cat (abdomen). License checked 2026-10-09 via the Sketchfab API. Its material labels are partly wrong: "Pancreas" is the spleen, the pancreas is one of the "Liver" objects and "Stomach" includes the abdominal esophagus and descending duodenum. scripts/build-cat-visceral.ts and scripts/ct/cat_visceral.py use the liver, stomach, small intestine, colon, spleen, pancreas (body and left lobe), kidneys, urinary bladder and abdominal great vessels: surfaces closed by voxel morphology, split, registered to the cat skeleton and decimated. The right pancreatic lobe, the rectum and the thoracic great vessels are modelled (fidelity "modeled").

name: Diffusion Tensor Imaging White Matter Atlas for the Domestic Feline (Cornell eCommons)
notes: MRI population template of domestic cats (Johnson PJ, Barry E, Luh W, Raj A, Cerda-Gonzalez S, 2019, Cornell eCommons, handle 1813/58775.2). CC0. scripts/ct/cat_brain.py meshes the T1 template and splits cerebrum, cerebellum and brainstem by watershed at the transverse fissure and the fourth ventricle; scripts/ct/cat_visceral.py fits it into the cranial cavity of the skull scan.

name: "Skelet jonge koe | skeleton young cow (800-1000)" by Archeologiemuseum Huis van Hilde (Sketchfab)
notes: Photogrammetry (model by Kees Zwaan) of the mounted skeleton of a heifer of 1.5-2 years, withers 1.07 m, found at Wijk aan Zee in 1970 (collection Huis van Hilde, PNH 11492-01). License checked 2026-10-10 via the Sketchfab API. The scan is one fused surface with the stand and support wires; scripts/build-cow-skeletal.ts cuts it into bones with a seeded watershed along the joint creases, keeps the left side and the median bones and mirrors the right side. The mount lacks the carpus and metacarpus of both thoracic limbs, most of the tail and part of the sternum, and its ribs are broken: ribs 1-3 and 10-13, sternebrae 6-7, the xiphoid and caudal vertebrae 3-18 are modeled. Because of the share-alike licence the skeletal GLB is CC BY-SA 4.0.

name: "Metacarpo de vaca/buey - VIRTARMED" by Grupo PRINMA, Universidad de Granada (Sketchfab)
notes: Scan of an adult ox metacarpus (19th century, Cuarto Real de Santo Domingo, Granada) with age-related exostoses on the dorsal face of the distal end. License checked 2026-10-10 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-cow-skeletal.ts scales it to 0.88 of the heifer's metatarsus and sets it between the modeled carpus and the digits.

name: "Bovine Rumen" by OVCanatomy, Ontario Veterinary College (Sketchfab)
notes: Model of a fixed bovine stomach by Joshua Antunes (OVC anatomy, University of Guelph), with windows cut into the rumen, omasum and abomasum. License checked 2026-10-10 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-cow-visceral.ts cuts the fused surface into rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum along the grooves between them and scripts/ct/cow_visceral.py places it in the abdomen of the cow skeleton (scaled from the diaphragm to the pelvic inlet).

name: "Whole Cow Heart Fixed" by Visible Heart Lab, University of Minnesota (Sketchfab)
notes: Artec Space Spider scan of a perfusion-fixed bovine heart. License checked 2026-10-10 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/ct/cow_visceral.py places it with its long axis from the base (ventral to T4) to the apex (on the sternum at the 5th rib); its roll about that axis is not known from the scan.

name: "Cow" by Thunk3D (Sketchfab)
notes: 3D scan of a sculpted dairy cow (one closed surface with one whole horn and a stump). License checked 2026-10-10 via the Sketchfab API. scripts/build-cow-integumentary.ts registers it onto the cow skeleton (legs and tail along their axes, trunk, neck and head by a thin-plate-spline warp and a similarity), inflates it over the bones, muscles and organs and cuts out the udder, the horn (mirrored for the other side) and the hooves below the coronary band (fidelity "modeled"; hooves "illustrative", without the interdigital cleft).
